niche_preference_profile: This user prefers interfaces that feel complete, structured, and easy to scan, with enough visible settings or content to feel fully functional. They generally like light or airy themes, clear hierarchy, centered or balanced titles, and concise copy. They favor layouts with well-separated sections, strong content completeness, and visible controls/actions, but they also dislike clutter, excessive chrome, and overly verbose or instructional presentation. In alert/modal contexts, they prefer polished, specific, trustworthy messaging with clear next steps and restrained visual noise.

criteria.description: Prefers screens that show a fuller, more complete set of settings or options rather than sparse or underfilled layouts.
Prefers interfaces with clearly separated, well-grouped sections and strong organizational boundaries.
Prefers pages that feel information-rich and operational, with enough visible items to feel finished and useful.
Prefers layouts that distribute content evenly across the screen and avoid large empty areas.
Prefers strong hierarchy with obvious titles, section headers, and a clear flow from headline to content to action.
Prefers short, direct, benefit-led or explanatory copy over verbose, instructional, or overly descriptive text.
Prefers lighter top bars, less branding noise, and less decorative UI chrome competing with the main content.
Prefers a clearly emphasized main action, especially when the task is a setup or confirmation flow.
Prefers controls that are clearly present in context, such as toggles, chevrons, and per-item actions that make the screen feel actionable.
Prefers interfaces that feel refined, official, and credible rather than generic, unfinished, or overly utilitarian.
Prefers alerts and modal copy that state the exact status, include concrete details, and tell the user what to do next.
Prefers screens with fewer competing elements, less clutter, and less distracting background content.
